A1.justification: Both complete PDFs describe UVGS and include readable methods, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary material. Corresponding content can be matched despite rearrangement and revised illustrations.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction, compression, generation, inpainting, and ablation results in the main text and supplement.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and reports revised quantitative and qualitative generation comparisons.

M1.justification: The spherical mapping, opacity-based top-K selection, branched forward/inverse networks, MSE and LPIPS losses, and autoencoder/diffusion pipelines remain unchanged. The supplementary algorithm and architecture support the same procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions cover Objaverse-derived objects, ShapeNet cars, complex objects, and real-world scenes across the same tasks. ShapeNet experiments already appear in v1's supplement; their explicit mention in v3's main text does not add coverage.

E2.justification: GaussianCube is added to the qualitative text-conditioned comparisons in main Figure 7 and supplementary Figure 7 of v3. It already participated in quantitative and unconditional comparisons. The quantitative comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Reported training budgets, UV resolutions, metrics, and evaluation sample counts remain unchanged. However, v1 separately identifies a fine-tuned ShapeNet variant, UVGS-S; v3 removes that row and labels the baseline comparisons as ShapeNet-cars. The PDFs do not resolve whether evaluation conditions changed or earlier attribution was clarified.

E4.justification: Revised GaussianCube car panels add close-ups identifying symmetry inconsistencies in main Figure 6 and supplementary Figure 6. This provides a limited qualitative error-analysis refinement. Layer-count, resolution, branching, interpolation, and scene analyses otherwise remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without seeds, repeated-run counts, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. No statistical uncertainty reporting is added.

E6.justification: Tables 2 and 4 substantially revise generation comparisons: Get3D FID/KID changes from 68.95/4.38 to 53.17/4.19 and GaussianCube from 48.44/4.89 to 34.67/3.72, reversing their KID ordering. DiffTF FID and several CLIP scores also change. UVGS's headline scores remain 26.20/3.24 and 32.62, but the UVGS-S row reporting 32.87/3.73 disappears. GaussianCube and LGM qualitative examples are added or replaced. Benchmark-attribution ambiguity prevents interpreting these as same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The Gaussian definitions, spherical-coordinate mapping, network equations, and reconstruction and diffusion objectives are retained. No new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about structured UVGS, compact Super UVGS, compatibility with pretrained image models, compression, generation, and inpainting.

C2.justification: The explanations involving spatial coherence and attribute-specific processing remain stable. Both versions retain the limitations concerning washed-out appearance, single-layer representation of complex geometry, and inefficient use of empty pixels, alongside the same proposed extensions.

D1.justification: v3 makes dataset attribution more explicit for generation figures and baseline comparisons, while removing the description of fine-tuning associated with UVGS-S. Network, normalization, optimizer, hardware, training-time, and caption-generation details otherwise match.

R1.justification: v3 adds Geometry Image Diffusion and An Object Is Worth 64x64 Pixels, with a related-work paragraph discussing mesh cutting and UV-island selection. This modestly expands positioning relative to image-based mesh generation; the broader related-work account remains stable.

P1.justification: v3 tightens wording throughout the introduction, methods, and experiments while retaining the section sequence and narrative. It changes the displayed author name from Arthur Chen to Kefan Chen and adds acknowledgements.

P2.justification: The visual presentation is extensively revised: diagrams and renderings become sharper, comparison panels add columns and close-ups, and the supplementary conditional comparison is rebuilt as a tall ten-row grid. The complex-object reconstruction figure is also redisplayed in the supplement, and numerous figures and tables are resized or repositioned.

improvement.justification: v3 improves visual clarity, adds relevant prior work and qualitative comparisons, and reconciles GaussianCube's conflicting main/supplementary CLIP scores to 30.34. However, removing the separately identified UVGS-S result while labeling comparisons as ShapeNet-cars leaves the relationship between central benchmark results unexplained. These presentation and contextual gains coexist with uncertainty about the interpretability of the revised empirical evidence, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
